title: Webb County Commissioners Weigh $400,000 Veterans Grant and Water Machines for Colonias
excerpt: Webb County commissioners took up a $400,000 veterans grant application, air-to-water machines for colonias and a Medical Examiner tracking system.
content:
The Webb County Commissioners Court took up three items Monday, Nov. 23, that would touch veterans, colonia residents and the Medical Examiner's Office: a $400,000 state grant application to expand the county's Veterans Treatment Program, a request to seek vendors for machines that make drinking water from air, and a $12,800-a-year system to track the deceased.

The court was asked to authorize submitting a Texas Veterans Commission Fund for Veterans' Assistance cost-reimbursement grant, in an amount not to exceed $400,000, for the Veterans Treatment Program. The grant requires no county match and would have no impact on the general fund, according to the county agenda. The money would expand the program's capacity and financial assistance for up to 30 participants, with case management, counseling and help with utility, mortgage and rent payments. The program serves veterans in eight counties — Dimmit, Jim Hogg, Jim Wells, Maverick, Starr, Val Verde, Webb and Zapata — including counties with few resources of their own.

The Veterans Treatment Program is a regional veterans treatment court at 4101 Juarez Ave. in Laredo, run on the drug-court model for veterans whose service-related post-traumatic stress, traumatic brain injury, substance use or mental-health condition affected their criminal conduct. It is currently funded by a Texas Veterans Commission regional grant and a federal SAMHSA grant. In September, Gov. Greg Abbott awarded Webb County $300,000 for the Veterans Treatment Court, plus $176,000 for transportation services, as part of more than $5.8 million in grants to South Texas veterans groups. The Nov. 23 item is a new application, not that award.

The court was also asked to authorize the Purchasing Agent to advertise a request for proposals for atmospheric water generators for the Webb County Atmospheric Water Project, funded through the Southwest Border Regional Commission's Economic and Infrastructure Development Grant Program. The machines extract moisture from the air, then filter and treat it to produce drinking water for underserved colonias along State Highway 59 and in South Laredo. The request would cover furnishing, delivery, installation and commissioning, including filtration and treatment components, replacement filters, warranties and maintenance.

The Medical Examiner's Office asked the court to approve a professional services agreement of up to $12,800 a year with MorgueBoard LLC for a decedent tracker system. The agenda says the system would modernize how the office handles decedent intake and release and standardize its tracking procedure.

The court was asked to act on the items at Monday's meeting. The outcome of the votes was not confirmed before publication — the county had not yet posted minutes for the Nov. 23 meeting. What to watch next: whether the veterans grant application is submitted, when the water-machine request for proposals opens, and how quickly the machines could reach the colonias.

Also on the agenda: ratification of more than $2.76 million in payments to SERVPRO for flood mitigation at the Billy Hall Administrative Building after the July 2026 flood, covered by insurance, plus a $707,873 permanent-repair contract; reallocations of federal ARPA money for the La Presa water extension; and a vote on creating the Binational Transformation City Public Improvement District.

Update — Nov. 26, 2026: KGNS reported the Commissioners Court approved submitting the $400,000 Texas Veterans Commission grant application for the Veterans Treatment Program. If awarded, the funding could help veterans with rent, mortgage and utility payments, for up to 30 participants across Webb County and seven other counties. The court also approved the Medical Examiner's Office contract with MorgueBoard LLC for the decedent tracking system.
